analysis:
The PR adds an experimental dev-branch release lane (.github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml, not supplied) that publishes ad-hoc signed builds named X.Y.Z-dev.branch.N to the dev coordinator. Supplied changes:
- scripts/check-release-version.sh:40 widens the accepted dev version regex to allow `branch.`.
- scripts/install.sh adds a relaxed designated requirement (`identifier "io.darkbloom.provider"` only). It is chosen from the version marker in select_provider_identity (~lines 59-69). verify_staged_app_signature defaults to it (~line 108).
- docs/operations/provider-release.md documents the lane. docs-impact-rules.json adds the new workflow and test script to the release rule.
Finding: the installer's signature-pin downgrade depends only on an API-supplied version string. The "prod never served pre-release" claim is a comment, not an enforced control. See scripts/install.sh:65 head.
Coverage limits and follow-ups for later passes:
- The workflow YAML and scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py were not provided, so credential isolation ("no secret in the compile job"), the dispatch-on-master restriction and branch-ref handling are unverified.
- The self-updater (ProviderCore+AutoUpdate) was not seen; check whether it uses the same relaxed requirement.
- The doc says dev and prod installs share the bundle id, the fan helper io.darkbloom.fan-helper (T-044/T-045) and the Hugging Face cache. Check whether the helper's client-validation requirement would accept an ad-hoc signed io.darkbloom.provider binary.
- A branch build becomes "latest" for all dev providers (auto-update) and registers a code_directory_hash in the dev App Attest qualification registry. This is dev-scoped, but check the dev-to-prod separation (TB-011, T-054).

findings.detail: select_provider_identity now picks DARKBLOOM_PRERELEASE_DESIGNATED_REQUIREMENT (`identifier "io.darkbloom.provider"` only) whenever the version contains `-dev.` or `-staging.`. That version comes from the same /v1/releases/latest response that supplies the URL and hashes. The only guard is a comment saying a prod coordinator is never served a pre-release version. The installer does not enforce this, even though PRODUCTION_COORD_URL is defined in the same file. A compromised or misconfigured release feed, or a prod install pointed at a non-prod coordinator, can return a `-dev.` version. The installer then accepts any ad-hoc signed bundle claiming that identifier, with no Developer ID or team-OU check. This removes the Developer ID check that backs the bundle-hash and URL checks. It also weakens the binary-integrity assumptions in T-013, T-034 and A-011 for an installer that holds provider keys and decrypted prompts. The new dev-branch lane makes self-signed builds from arbitrary branches routinely publishable, which raises the exposure. Fix: apply the relaxed requirement only when the effective coordinator is explicitly a non-production host (not PRODUCTION_COORD_URL). Alternatively, make it a build-time property of the dev installer snapshot that the prod installer cannot reach.
findings.title: Installer drops the Apple-anchor signature pin based on an API-supplied version string
